title: Hydrogen atom total energies
action: Implement a self-consistent spherical Kohn-Sham solver that uses the interpolation formulas for exchange-correlation energy and potentials for the homogeneous spin-polarized electron liquid (given in the problem statement). Compute the total energy of the hydrogen atom (Z=1) in the LSD (ζ self-consistent) and LD (ζ=0) approximations. Write a CSV file with two rows.
description: Total energies of the hydrogen atom in LSD and LD approximations.
output_schema: Two rows. Columns: method (string, either 'LSD' or 'LD'), total_energy_eV (float, negative, in eV).

title: Sodium atom total energies
action: Using the same Kohn-Sham solver, compute the total energy of the sodium atom (Z=11) in the LSD and LD approximations. Write a CSV file with two rows, reporting energies in Rydbergs.
description: Total energies of the sodium atom in LSD and LD approximations, in Rydbergs.
output_schema: Two rows. Columns: method (string, either 'LSD' or 'LD'), total_energy_Ry (float, negative, in Rydbergs).

title: Sodium cohesive energy
action: Read the sodium atom energies from step_02. Compute the improved LSD cohesive energy of sodium using Tong's published LD cohesive energy (1.39 eV/atom) and a correlation-energy interpolation correction (0.07 eV) as: E_coh^LSD = 1.39 eV + (E_atom^LD − E_atom^LSD) + 0.07 eV, where E_atom^LD and E_atom^LSD are the total energies from step_02 converted to eV. Write the resulting value in eV to a text file.
description: Improved LSD cohesive energy of sodium (in eV), computed by adding spin-polarization and correlation corrections to Tong's LD result.
output_schema: Single floating-point number (in eV, positive) in plain text.
